chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'A man has a make-up prayer (qada) from the month of Ramadan, and he rises in the morning and does not eat until the afternoon prayer. Is it permissible for him to count it as make-up from the month of Ramadan?' He said: 'Yes.' The explanation in this report is one of two things: either we interpret it as permissible (jawaz) and the first report as indicating excellence and preference (fadl and istihbab), or the meaning of 'until the afternoon' is the beginning of the afternoon time, which is after solar noon by the amount of time it takes to pray four units of the obligatory noon prayer, because that is the beginning of the afternoon time as we explained. And his statement in the first report 'after the sun has passed' refers to the time that extends from this point until the end of the afternoon time, or significantly after it.
ai.seo_question: Can a person make up missed Ramadan fasts during the day without eating until afternoon, and is it considered valid from Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits counting a day of *Qada* (make-up) fast as valid for Ramadan if one abstains from food until the beginning of the afternoon (*Asr*) prayer, a ruling derived from the specific definition of *Asr* as starting after the sun passes its zenith by the time required for four obligatory units of prayer. The text further elucidates the juristic nuance between this ruling being merely permissible (*Jawaz*) versus preferred (*Istihbab*), and clarifies the temporal boundary of 'afternoon' to distinguish it from the later part of the prayer time. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise temporal definitions in ritual law and the flexibility within the Hanafi-Shia comparative jurisprudence regarding the validity of make-up fasts.
